title: Post-deploy observation labbook
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for observations, quick playbook updates, and one-off fixes after a canary flip. Not a final runbook — this is my lab notebook for the next 48h following the 2025-02-12 canary that bumped model from redwood-v2-small -> redwood-v2-medium (quantized).

TOP-LEVEL NOTES
- Canary cohort: 5% global traffic, subset: eu-west-1 + stg clients flagged in tenant list canary-2025-02.
- Primary risk vectors: tokenized prompt length distribution shift, KV cache pressure on longer sequences, minor latency regression under burst traffic.
- Immediate ask: watch p95 latency, error-rate by route, and cost-per-token drift (token billing anomalies seen in last two experiments).

QUICK OBSERVATIONS (first 12h)
- p50 stable, p95 up ~12% (baseline p95 230ms -> 259ms). Not catastrophic but above expected buffer.
- Small increase in transient 5xx spikes, concentrated on /chat/completions route for tenants using function-calling. Correlated with unusual patterns in KV hit ratio dropping from 0.82 -> 0.63.
- GPU memory pressure: a handful of pods saw ephemeral GPU OOMs during long-seq replays (logs: runtime-gpu-3@2025-02-12:22:17). Appears tied to a change in attention cache retention logic in PR#2134.
- Cost-per-token: synthetic telemetry shows 7% increase for canary cohort; need to confirm on billing pipeline aggregation (possible double-counting slug issue).

IMMEDIATE MITIGATIONS (if regressions worsen)
- Ramp down cohort to 1% (r-i control plane -> roll traffic --cohort canary-2025-02 --set 1%).
- Pin affected tenants back to redwood-v2-small using tenant pin API (examples below).
- Turn on short-circuit fallback to v2-small for any request with len(prompt_tokens) > 2048.

PINNING EXAMPLE (CLI)
- pin tenant: r-i tenants pin --tenant-id t-3492 --model redwood-v2-small --expires 2025-03-01
- verify: r-i tenants describe t-3492 | jq '.pinned_model'

ROLLBACK TRIGGERS (suggested)
- sustained p95 > baseline + 25% for 30m OR sudden jump in 5xx > 0.8% sustained for 15m.
- KV cache hit ratio drop below 0.6 for 20 consecutive minutes across >30% of pods.
- Any GPU OOM observed on >=2 distinct hosts within 1h.

CHECKLIST (first 6 hours)
- [ ] Confirm Canary cohort traffic split in Console and CLI (owner: Amira)
- [ ] Snapshot top-20 tenants by qps and latency (owner: Derek)
- [ ] Export nightly billing sample for canary cohort (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Attach debug logs for runtime-gpu-3 and runtime-gpu-5 to PR#2134 thread
- [ ] Post a status note to #infra-canary with observed metrics (use template below)

SLACK UPDATE TEMPLATE (post to #infra-canary)
- short: "Canary update 02/12 — p95 +12% (eu-west cohort). Holding at 5%. Investigating KV hit regression; ramping to 1% if conditions worsen. — Amira"
- long: include bullet list of p50/p95, 5xx rate, KV hit ratio, any pinned tenant list, CLI commands executed, links to logs/PRs.

TELEMETRY QUERIES (ad hoc)
- p95 by route: metrics.query('latency.p95', route='/chat/completions', timeframe=60m, cohort='canary-2025-02')
- KV hit ratio: logs.search('kv_cache_hit_rate', hostgroup='runtime-gpu-*', timeframe=120m)
- 5xx spikes: infra.alerts('error_rate', threshold=0.8, timeframe=15m)

DEEP-DIVE HYPOTHESES
1) Cache retention bug: PR#2134 changed LRU eviction threshold causing rapid churn for longer sequences — explains KV hit ratio drop and GPU OOMs.
   - Quick test: deploy a debug build with old eviction thresholds to a single canary pod and replay long prompts.
2) Quantization path increases compute per-token for medium model under certain sequence lengths — leads to p95 increase localized to longer prompts.
   - Quick test: run model profiler on representative prompt set (from /analyses/prompt-length-distrib) and compare kernel runtimes.
3) Billing pipeline double-counts tokens when fallback and streaming interleave — cost spike artifact.
   - Quick test: enable additional debug-tag on events to trace token accounting for canary users.

ONE-OFF COMMANDS / LOG SNIPPETS
- check pod OOMs: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=OOMKilled -n runtime | grep runtime-gpu
- attach logs: r-i logs --pod runtime-gpu-3 --since 2h > /tmp/gpu3.log
- quick SQL to sample tenant usage: SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) FROM billing_events WHERE ts > '2025-02-12' AND tenant_tag = 'canary-2025-02' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum(tokens) DESC LIMIT 50;

NOTES TO SELF / TODOs
- Follow up with research team about profiler results (assign to Derek for kernel-level breakdown).
- Add a temporary instrumentation flag to runtime that emits per-request token-accounting-id so billing pipeline can trace end-to-end.
- Ask product if any customers in cohort are running production-critical flows that can't tolerate short blips; customer-success contact list is small but include 3 names (Priya has the list).
- Draft postmortem template if we end up rollbacks — keep it short: timeline, telemetry, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, follow-ups.

OUTSTANDING QUESTIONS
- Is the LRU setting change intentional for long-term performance? (Ping @infra-owners)
- Can we reproduce GPU OOM locally with short repro script? I have a sample prompt set at /home/amira/repro/long-prompts-2025-02.txt
- Should we add an automated canary thermostat that throttles traffic by observed delta in p95 rather than static %? (engineering discussion item)

REFERENCE LINKS
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2134
- Linear ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/RI-4821-canary-metrics-collection
- Quick prompt distrib CSV: gs://redwood-analytics/canary/prompt-lengths/2025-02-12.csv

FINAL: This doc will be updated as I run reproductions. If I pin a tenant I'll append the tenant id and timestamp below (useful short audit):
- pinned: t-3492 @ 2025-02-12T23:48Z -> redwood-v2-small (reason: GPU OOM observed)
- ramp actions: 2025-02-13T01:10Z -> cohort reduced to 2% (manual)

End of labbook entry (Amira)
